subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Silicon Carbide: Extreme Conditions
description: A short lesson to help you apply Silicon Carbide: Extreme Conditions.

hook.text: Electric vehicle motors run at hundreds of volts. Silicon carbide handles it with ease.

buildup.text: SiC has a 3.3 eV band gap and excellent thermal conductivity. Heat flows out fast.

discovery.text: SiC MOSFETs cut switching losses in half compared to silicon — boosting EV range.

twist.text: Growing SiC crystals is much harder than silicon — wafers cost ten times as much.

climax.text: Tesla's Model 3 inverter uses SiC transistors — a major reason for its efficiency.

punchline.text: Expensive to make but worth every watt saved in an electric drivetrain.

quiz.question: Why is silicon carbide preferred in electric vehicle inverters?
options: It is cheaper than silicon for high-volume production
Its wide band gap and thermal conductivity cut switching losses, extending EV range
It can be doped more easily than silicon
